attacks.name: new_evidence_round2_relitigation_refused_intended
attacks.note: OQ-T13/relitigation: admit() has zero round-awareness; a round-2 exhibit unrelated to round-1's dispute is admitted exactly like a round-0 exhibit. Intended behaviour (evidence frozen after round 1, per the approved dispute design) is NOT implemented in evidence.py today.

writable_vs_resolvable.how: candle_text exhibits carry explicit high/close fields; the model is asked about 'high price'.

admit()/tiering has no concept of 'window'; the LLM is asked to compare two timestamps' 5-minute buckets itself -- arithmetic, not reading comprehension, so reliability is unverified per-case rather than guaranteed by code.

writable_vs_resolvable.clause: UTC deadline pinned against literal 'PST' string
writable_vs_resolvable.how: code: evidence_cutoff/time fields are already ISO8601 UTC; J.lint() rejects non-UTC time fields outright (see lint gate test).

nothing in admit()/judge_element()/decide() distinguishes 'early' resolution from 'resolution at deadline'; the term sheet CAN say it (custom_definitions string) but no code path enforces 'YES fires the instant it's true, NO only after window_end' -- decide() is stateless per-call, not an early-stopping scheduler.

writable_vs_resolvable.clause: Fallback requires a NAMED second confirming source (Kraken), not just 'another source'
writable_vs_resolvable.how: implemented by mapping Kraken to a lower CLASS_RANK tier so judge_element()'s existing tier-fallthrough triggers it -- but this is a repurposed mechanism (tiers model 'better evidence class', not 'fallback source'); nothing stops a maker writing fallback rules the 3 class-rank slots (primary/data/wire/outlet) can't express (e.g. 'need 2-of-3 fallbacks').

writable_vs_resolvable.clause: VOID when fewer than two of the three named sources can be checked at all
writable_vs_resolvable.how: F.void_no_two_sources() (mirrored in evidence.py's own no_data_available/COULDNT_CHECK path) is checked BEFORE calling the model: fewer than two distinct checkable publishers -> VOID, deterministically, never a silent model-side NO.

writable_vs_resolvable.clause: Fork/ticker rule (whichever ticker each exchange itself lists as BTC)
writable_vs_resolvable.how: nothing in judge.py/evidence.py has any notion of 'ticker redirect' or 'which asset a renamed/forked ticker refers to'; it is pure natural-language text the LLM reads cold, with no code-level fact check backing it (contrast REVISION_WINDOW_V1, which IS code-checked).

writable_vs_resolvable.clause: Pinned judge model + ordered fallback list
writable_vs_resolvable.how: J.call() dispatches on the model string; MODELS env/param already supports an ordered list.
writable_vs_resolvable.test: harness MODELS=claude:haiku,claude:sonnet (not exercised live to save budget)

writable_vs_resolvable.clause: Revision window for corrected exchange data
writable_vs_resolvable.how: J.apply_revision_window()/REVISION_WINDOW_V1 clause is exactly this; our term sheet omits the clause itself today (gap B candidate -- see below) but the code exists.
J.decide(): ALL-rule NO is the default on any not_met/insufficient/missing element.

gap_b_candidates.name: per-element numeric threshold/comparator field
gap_b_candidates.note: evidence.py/judge.py elements are a free-text 'q' string; the resolver COULD check a structured {field: high, op: >=, value: 126210.50} comparison deterministically (no LLM, no quote-verification risk) exactly like framework 1's mechanical resolver is supposed to -- but the term-sheet schema this harness runs on has no field for it, so even a disciplined maker is forced to express a numeric trigger as a prose question an LLM has to parse.

gap_b_candidates.name: round_no / evidence-freeze flag on exhibits
gap_b_candidates.note: OQ-T13: admit() could check 'is this exhibit new since round 1', but exhibits have no field for round number and no code reads one.

gap_b_candidates.name: revision window pairing beyond one clause flag
gap_b_candidates.note: REVISION_WINDOW_V1 exists in CLAUSES but the canonical term sheet never listed it -- a writable gap in the OTHER direction: the resolver can check it, the maker just didn't ask for it.
